extraction.name: VQAonline
extraction.description: A fully authentic visual question answering dataset sourced from online question-answering communities (Stack Exchange), containing natural language questions, context, images, and accepted answers.
extraction.creator: Chongyan Chen, Mengchen Liu, Noel Codella, Yunsheng Li, Lu Yuan, and Danna Gurari
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by scraping data from the online question-answering platform Stack Exchange. The authors collected examples containing a natural language question, natural language context, an image, and at least one answer, and kept only examples where the asker marked an accepted answer. They then filtered out low-quality examples, multi-image examples, visual answers, and examples whose images could not be downloaded.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Examples without an accepted answer were removed. Examples with multiple images, visual answers, or images that could not be downloaded were also removed.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Publicly available Stack Exchange archive data in XML format hosted at archive.org/details/stackexchange, spanning August 2010 to November 2022.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Two filtering steps were applied: removed visual questions with scores of 0 or less for either the question or answer, excluded visual questions with multiple images or visual answers, and removed examples whose images could not be downloaded. All images were converted to PNG format for consistency.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Collected only examples with four components (question, context, image, at least one answer) and an accepted answer; removed low-quality VQAs based on post scores; excluded multiple-image and visual-answer examples; removed undownloadable images; converted images to PNG.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For user-intention annotations, crowdworkers labeled each visual question with one primary intent using provided instructions, taxonomy definitions, and examples. Two independent workers annotated each of 105 randomly selected VQAs, and a third worker broke ties when the first two disagreed. Final labels were majority-vote labels from three crowdsourced annotations per visual question.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk; a home-grown web-based interface was used for human evaluation of model answers.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For user-intention labeling, disagreements between two annotators were resolved by a third worker, and the final label was the majority vote from three labels per VQA. The authors also reported agreement accuracy and Cohen's kappa across four rounds of taxonomy refinement.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 for user-intention annotations; 6 model-generated answers were rated per VQA in the human evaluation study.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: For user-intention annotations: three crowdworkers from Amazon Mechanical Turk, restricted to workers located in the United States with more than 500 HITs and over 95% approval rating. For human evaluation: ten domain experts, each in one of ten topics, all located in the United States and with at least a Master's degree in a related field.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-3.5 was used to bootstrap initial free-form user-intention categories; DeepSolo was used to detect text in images; LLaMA2 was used as an evaluation metric for answer correctness.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is publicly shared at https://vqaonline.github.io/. The paper does not specify a versioning schedule, maintainer policy, or deprecation policy.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Geography/country of users and annotators (e.g., United States, India, Europe, Egypt); language-related content in questions; user-generated visual questions from various countries. The paper also notes multilingual VQAs.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors state that improved models for this dataset could benefit community question-answering platforms, learning-assistance VQA tools for children, virtual assistants, visual dialog and query, and visual search and browsing. They also discuss potential use for studying hallucination in authentic use cases.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas because Stack Exchange users have access to mobile devices and the Internet. Geographic representation is unbalanced, with more users from the US, India, and Europe and fewer from countries like Egypt. The dataset also has a long-tail topic distribution.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited by its reliance on Stack Exchange users and may not generalize to populations without access to mobile devices and the Internet. It has a long-tail distribution across topics, and the authors note that some topics have very few examples. The paper also notes that standard VQA evaluation metrics are ill-suited because answers are much longer than in prior datasets.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and test splits are provided. The dataset supports few-shot learning and benchmarking of VQA models. The authors also use it for human evaluation of model answers and analysis of evaluation metrics.
